blocks.html: Let \(X\) be a proper smooth scheme over a field \(k\). The de Rham cohomology of \(X/k\), \(H_{\mathrm{DR}}^*(X/k) := H^*(X, \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k})\), is the abutment of the Hodge spectral sequence

It is known that, if \(k\) has characteristic zero, (0.1) degenerates at \(E_1\): for \(X\) projective, this follows from Hodge theory, and the proper case reduces to the projective case by Chow's lemma and resolution of singularities (cf. [5, 5.5]).

The first proof of this fact not using Hodge theory was given by Faltings [8], as an application of his theory of the existence of a Hodge-Tate decomposition for the \(p\)-adic étale cohomology of proper smooth varieties over local fields of unequal characteristic.

If \(k\) has characteristic \(p>0\), it can happen that (0.1) does not degenerate at \(E_1\) (cf. Mumford [22] and 2.5 (i)). However, Kato has recently shown [14] that, for \(k\) perfect of characteristic \(p>0\) and \(X\) projective and smooth over \(k\), if one assumes that \(X\) has dimension \(<p\) and lifts over the ring \(W(k)\) of Witt vectors of \(k\), then this "pathological" phenomenon does not occur. Fontaine and Messing [10] extended this result to the proper case, and deduced, by a standard argument, the degeneration of (0.1) in characteristic zero. This second proof uses crystalline techniques.

We give here an elementary proof of a result more precise than that of Kato and Fontaine-Messing, which is the following. Suppose \(k\) perfect, of characteristic \(p>0\), and let \(X\) be a smooth \(k\)-scheme (of arbitrary dimension, and not necessarily proper). Let \(X'\) be deduced from \(X\) by the extension of scalars \(k \xrightarrow{\lambda} k\), \(\lambda \mapsto \lambda^p\), and \(F : X \to X'\) the relative Frobenius (1.1). We prove that each smooth lifting \(\tilde X\) of \(X\) over the ring \(W_2(k)\) of Witt vectors of length 2 determines an isomorphism
\[ \tag{0.2} \varphi_{\tilde X} : \bigoplus_{0 \leqslant i < p} \Omega^i_{X'/k}[-i] \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \tau_{<p}\, F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/k} \]

in the derived category \(D(X')\). It follows, by a count of dimensions, that if \(X\) admits a smooth lifting \(\tilde X\) over \(W_2(k)\), and is moreover assumed proper and of dimension \(<p\), the spectral sequence (0.1) degenerates at \(E_1\).

Here is the principle of the construction of \(\varphi_{\tilde X}\). Let \(\sigma : W_2(k) \to W_2(k)\) be the lifting \((\lambda_0, \lambda_1) \mapsto (\lambda_0^p, \lambda_1^p)\) of the automorphism \(\lambda \mapsto \lambda^p\) of \(k\) and \(\tilde X'\) deduced from \(\tilde X\) by the extension of scalars \(\sigma\). If \(F\) lifts to \(\tilde F : \tilde X \to \tilde X'\), the homomorphism \(\tilde F^* : \Omega^1_{\tilde X'/W_2(k)} \to \tilde F_* \Omega^1_{\tilde X/W_2(k)}\) provides, after division by \(p\), a morphism of complexes

inducing on \(\mathscr{H}^1\) the Cartier isomorphism \(C^{-1}\) (1.2) (this idea, which goes back to Mazur's article [20], has already been very widely exploited). If \(\tilde F_1\) and \(\tilde F_2\) are two liftings, their "difference" is a homomorphism from \(\Omega^1_{X'/k}\) to \(F_* \mathcal{O}_X\). It provides a homotopy between the arrows \(f_1\) and \(f_2\) associated with \(\tilde F_1\) and \(\tilde F_2\). These homotopies satisfy a transitivity condition. This makes it possible to globalize the construction by means of a covering of \(X\) by open sets on which \(F\) lifts. One thus obtains the component \(\varphi^1\) of \(\varphi\). One defines the component \(\varphi^0\) as the arrow induced by \(F^*\), and one deduces the \(\varphi^i\) from \(\varphi^0\) and \(\varphi^1\) thanks to the multiplicative structure of the de Rham complex (it is here that the restriction \(i<p\) comes in).

This construction is explained in §2, after a brief review, in §1, of the definition of the relative Frobenius and the Cartier isomorphism. We also give, in §2, the "standard" argument allowing one to deduce from (0.2) the degeneration of (0.1) in characteristic zero. For \(X\) of dimension \(<p\), liftable over \(W_2(k)\), (0.2) provides a decomposition in \(D(X', \mathcal{O})\)

We show that one still has such a decomposition for \(X\) of dimension \(p\). Finally, we deduce from (0.2) a vanishing theorem of Kodaira type in characteristic \(p\): if \(X\) is a projective and smooth, equidimensional \(k\)-scheme, liftable over \(W_2(k)\), and if \(L\) is an ample invertible sheaf on \(X\), then
\[ H^j(X, \Omega^i_{X/k} \otimes L^{-1}) = 0 \quad \text{pour } i+j < \inf(p, \dim X). \]
This result and its proof are due to Michel Raynaud. The classical Kodaira-Akizuki-Nakano theorem in characteristic zero follows from it by the usual argument.

The obstruction to the existence of a decomposition of type (0.2) and the dependence of \(\varphi_{\tilde X}\) on \(\tilde X\) are studied in §3, where the construction of \(\varphi\) is taken up again over a base \(S\) of characteristic \(p>0\). We show in particular the following result: if \(X\) admits a lifting \(\tilde X\) over \(\mathbf{Z}/p^2\), if \(X\) is a smooth \(S\)-scheme and \(X'\) is its inverse image under the absolute Frobenius of \(S\), then \(X'\) admits a smooth lifting over \(\tilde S\) if and only if there exists an arrow \(\Omega^1_{X'/S}[-1] \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\) in \(D(X', \mathcal{O})\) inducing the Cartier isomorphism \(C^{-1}\) on \(\mathscr{H}^1\). An application to the degeneration of the relative Hodge spectral sequence is given in §4, where we also briefly treat the variant of the preceding results for the de Rham complex with logarithmic poles along a divisor with normal crossings.
